D001_m001.question:
I’ve always felt like my brain never really shuts off, but it’s gotten harder to keep up over the last six months—really, probably been building for years. At work, I’m juggling cases, documentation, meetings, and I constantly feel overwhelmed, even though I care so deeply about my clients. I know I’m smart and capable, but I’ll start writing a report and then notice I’ve jumped to three other tabs, answering emails I didn’t need to respond to yet, or I’ll get pulled in by a noise down the hall and lose my train of thought completely. It’s like my attention just drifts, even when I’m trying so hard to focus.

I’ve been told I talk a lot—I think I do. In team meetings, I’ll start explaining something and go on a tangent, not because I want to dominate the conversation, but because ideas keep popping up. My coworkers are kind, but I’ve noticed some exchange looks when I interrupt or jump in too fast.

I’ve been this way since I was a kid—teachers said I was bright but scattered, always fidgeting, blurting answers. Now, even at home, I’m never really still. I’ll start cleaning, then pick up a book, then remember a call to make—it’s like I’m being pulled in ten directions all the time.

A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
